verdict.reason: may interrupt a resource clients use by name (97%)

state:
An OpenTofu (Terraform) plan is about to be applied to an AWS account (one region). Running applications use these resources by name: they read and write objects, table items, queue messages, secrets and parameters, and invoke functions. Applying the plan carries out the resource changes below in dependency order. Replacing a resource destroys the old one and then creates the new one, unless the plan says the new one is created first (create_before_destroy). If a change fails, the apply stops there; the changes already made stay made.

aws_s3_bucket.b: bucket vaws-s19-data; holds 0 objects; versioning never enabled; force_destroy = true in the state
aws_s3_bucket.logs: bucket vaws-s19-logs; holds 20 objects; versioning never enabled; force_destroy = true in the state

Actions, in order:
1. Destroy aws_s3_bucket.b (it was removed from the configuration)

How these resources behave: Destroying an aws_s3_bucket that still holds objects or object versions fails unless force_destroy is true in the current state; a force_destroy = true set in the same plan does not apply to that destroy. With force_destroy = true in the state, every object and every version is deleted first.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
